headline: Recent news is polarised: Docklands vacancy has hit a record high while AI-driven lettings and supply-shortage forecasts dominate the core, against a backdrop of sharply higher gilt yields.
summary: The most material recent items are: CoStar reporting record Docklands Core vacancy of 18.6%; CoStar's forecast that UK office demand will outpace supply from mid-2027; continued AI-sector leasing (Anthropic, OpenAI, PromethiusAI) highlighted in JLL's Q2 review; and analysis showing 2025 office starts well below average, with refurbishments dominant. In the background, the 10-year gilt yield has climbed to 5.36% (Bank of England data), which is likely to weigh on investment pricing.
insights: [Sep/Oct 2026] Docklands Core vacancy reaches 18.6%, the highest since 2003. Canary Wharf landlords face pressure despite large deals (CoStar).
[2026] CoStar UK office forecast: demand to outpace supply from mid-2027, supporting prime rental growth (CoStar).
[Aug 2026] JLL Q2 review: TMT took 33% of take-up on a wave of AI occupiers; space under construction is at a five-year low (JLL).
[Aug 2026] 2025 office starts of ~4.8m sq ft were below the ~6.5m five-year average, with refurbishments ~two-thirds of starts (London Construction Magazine).
[Oct 2026] The 10-year gilt yield is at 5.36%, up ~107bp since February (Bank of England).

signals.title: Investment pricing under pressure
signals.rationale: Rising gilt yields are likely to delay the recovery in investment volumes and could push prime yields out.

signals.title: Counter-cyclical acquisitions in Docklands
signals.rationale: Record vacancy may create discounted entry points for long-term repositioning, for example to life sciences or residential.
